However, the cited evidence does not address multilayer interfaces, creep mechanisms, or the transition between diffusion- and dislocation-dominated deformation, leaving those premises unsupported.
premises: Severe lattice distortion in HEAs impedes long-range dislocation motion and promotes solid-solution strengthening.
Chemical short-range order (SRO) varies spatially in HEAs and influences dislocation activity.
SRO and lattice distortion are inversely coupled: stronger SRO reduces lattice distortion, weaker SRO amplifies it.
In HEA multilayers, interfaces with heterogeneous SRO and lattice distortion promote localized dislocation nucleation and create a gradient of plastic deformation.
The transition between diffusion-dominated and dislocation-mediated creep is determined by local SRO and lattice distortion.
